questions.q: Which column should you filter on for query performance when querying system.access.audit, per Databricks' own recommendation?
questions.explain: Databricks recommends filtering on event_date (a date column) rather than event_time (a timestamp), because the table's performance optimizations are built around event_date.

questions.q: What does the user_identity column in system.access.audit contain?
options: A struct with the acting user's email (and subjectName)
A list of every group the user belongs to
questions.explain: user_identity is a struct recording the identity of the user initiating the request, e.g. {"email": "user@domain.com", "subjectName": null}; source_ip_address is a separate column.

questions.q: In the query filtering on `request_params['full_name_arg'] = 'hr_catalog.silver.employees'`, what is request_params used for?
options: Setting the retention period for that query's results
Extracting a specific parameter (like the full table name) from the map of request details
Specifying which system table to query
questions.explain: request_params is a map column holding request-specific key/value details; indexing it with a key like full_name_arg narrows the audit query to events touching one specific object.

questions.q: Who can see unmasked values for request_params keys like view_definition and function_info?
options: No one — these values are permanently redacted for everyone
Any user with SELECT on system.access.audit
Account admins, or members of the databricks_pii_access account-level group
Only the user who originally performed the action
questions.explain: Keys that embed SQL definitions (function_info, view_definition, definition_json, managed_definition) are omitted from request_params unless the querying user is an account admin or in the databricks_pii_access group.

questions.q: What workspace_id value is recorded for account-level audit events?
options: The workspace's own numeric ID, same as workspace-level events
questions.explain: Account-level audit events record workspace_id as 0, distinguishing them from workspace-level events which carry the actual workspace's ID.
